newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India eases as political tensions rise.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India eases as political tensions rise.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished mildly lower on Thursday in nervous trade ahead of Friday's key confidence vote in parliament, dealers said.
They said the market was showing surprising resilience in the face of growing fears that the ruling United Front coalition would lose the vote and a new election would be held later this year.
"The local market is saying that the government will fall but the GDR market is saying something else," said a trader in London.
But he said the market was unsure about future direction, and would wait for the results of the vote on Friday. Volumes were limited in GDR trade on Thursday.

Indian shares ended weaker on news the Congress party had instructed its deputies to vote against the ruling coalition in the vote but the political situation remained unclear, dealers in Bombay said.

The Congress on March 30 withdrew crucial support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party centre-left coalition, sparking off the current political crisis and raising the prospect of mid-term elections.
An official of the ruling United Front coalition said on Thursday India can expect general elections in May or June under a caretaker government headed by Deve Gowda.
The key concern in the market was the future of the 1997/8 budget, which is yet to be passed by parliament.
A dealer said GDR prices had come off the lows in afternoon trade. Reliance managed a 52 cent gain to $16.25/17.25, while SBI ended 18 cents off at $20/21 and VSNL lost 17 cents to $17.75/18.75.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.50 point, or 0.68 percent, up at 73.91, with the premium over the local market at 19.69 percent from 18.45 percent on Wednesday.
Taiwanese GDRs fell back in line with local market losses, with the Capel Taiwan GDR Index down 2.13 points at 128.51, representing a discount to the local market of 4.11 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 2.15 points, or 3.32 percent, off at 62.61, a premium of 27.62 percent over the local market.
